title: Half-Bridge Converter (isolated)
summary: Galvanically isolated buck-derived converter; two switches drive the transformer primary across an input-capacitor divider, and a full-wave secondary rectifier feeds an LC output filter. The CCM ratio is n * D / 2, where n = N2/N1 is the turns ratio. The transformer is driven symmetrically (self-resetting) and there is no right-half-plane zero.

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive primary-side input bus rail feeding the switch totem-pole and the input-capacitor divider.

ports.name: sw_mid
ports.description: Switching-node midpoint between the two primary switches S1 (high side) and S2 (low side); one terminal of the transformer primary.

ports.name: cap_mid
ports.description: Midpoint of the two series input capacitors CB1/CB2 (sits at Vin/2); the other terminal of the transformer primary.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Isolated regulated output rail across the LC filter and load (secondary side).

ports.name: sec_gnd
ports.description: Secondary-side ground reference (output return), galvanically isolated from pri_gnd.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Complementary gate-drive commands for S1 and S2 (each on for duty D within its half-period, with dead-time) from the controller.

parameters.name: Vin
parameters.description: Primary-side input bus voltage (VB); the transformer primary swings +/- Vin/2 about the capacitor-divider midpoint.

parameters.name: fsw
parameters.description: Per-switch switching frequency; the output filter sees ripple at 2*fsw because both half-cycles deliver energy.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of each switch, defined as the on-time within its half switching period.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Power transformer turns ratio n = N2/N1 (secondary over primary).

parameters.name: C_B
parameters.description: Each of the two series input divider capacitors (CB1 = CB2 = C_B); their midpoint holds Vin/2.

parameters.name: r_B
parameters.description: Equivalent series resistance of each input divider capacitor; appears only in the input-impedance transfer function.

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Output inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term affecting the DC conversion ratio.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: turns_ratio
design_equations.description: Power transformer turns ratio definition (Alonso eq. 6.3).

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio
design_equations.description: Ideal CCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 6.9 lossless); the buck ratio D scaled by the turns ratio n, with the factor 1/2 because the primary sees only Vin/2 across the capacitor divider.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio including the output inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 6.9); the capacitor ESR does not affect the DC ratio because no DC current flows in C.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average output inductor current equals the load current in CCM (the LC filter keeps the output current continuous, as in a buck).

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 6.37); the buck ripple with the reflected primary voltage n*Vin/2.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM for an ideal capacitor (Alonso eq. 6.38); ESR adds r_C * dI_L on top. The 1/16 factor (vs. 1/8 for the buck) is because the output filter is refreshed twice per switching period (effective ripple frequency 2*fsw).

design_equations.name: rectifier_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through each secondary rectifier D1-D4 and the output inductor in CCM (Alonso summary).

design_equations.name: switch_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through each primary switch S1/S2 in CCM (Alonso summary); the reflected inductor peak current.

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across each primary switch (Alonso summary); with the two switches in a totem-pole across the bus, the off switch blocks the full input voltage Vin (plus any leakage spike). No reset winding is needed - the symmetric bidirectional drive self-resets the core.

design_equations.name: rectifier_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak reverse voltage across each secondary rectifier D1-D4 (Alonso summary).

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 6.40): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim. The factor 4 (vs. 2 for the buck/forward) follows from the doubled effective output ripple frequency 2*fsw.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 6.39).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = n / (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * k / D**2)),  k = 4 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 6.54-6.55); load-dependent, with the doubled-frequency factor k = 4*L*fsw/R_load.

design_equations.name: dcm_peak_inductor_current
design_equations.expression: i_pk = D * (n * Vin - 2 * Vout) / (4 * L * fsw)
design_equations.description: Peak inductor (and reflected switch) current in DCM (Alonso eq. 6.43 / DCM summary).

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.expression: Den(s) = L*C*(1 + r_C/R_load)*s**2 + (L/R_load + r_C*C + r_L*C + r_L*r_C*C/R_load)*s + (1 + r_L/R_load)
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below; identical to the buck and forward (a complex pole pair near 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C))), because the half-bridge is dynamically a buck seen through the transformer.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 6.21-6.22); the buck Gd(s) scaled to n*Vin/2 (= (Vout/D)*(1 + r_L/R_load)). Single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C), no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 6.23); the buck Gb(s) scaled by n/2, same dynamics as Gd(s).

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 6.33); identical to the buck and forward and independent of the turns ratio (the secondary side is a plain LC filter). Zo(0) approx r_L, Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Zi(s) = Z_B(s)*Z_C(s)/(Z_B(s) + Z_C(s)),  Z_B(s) = 2*r_B + 2/(C_B*s),  Z_C(s) = (R_load/(n**2*D**2)) * Den(s) / (1 + (R_load + r_C)*C*s)
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 6.24, 6.26-6.30): the passive input-capacitor divider Z_B in parallel with the active converter input Z_C. Z_C is the buck input impedance divided by n**2*D**2 (Z_C(0) = (R_load + r_L)/(n**2*D**2)), reflecting the n*D/2 stage gain.

control_notes: The half-bridge converter is dynamically a buck converter seen through the power transformer: two switches (S1/S2) drive the primary across an input-capacitor divider, and a full-wave secondary rectifier (D1-D4) feeds a continuous-current LC output filter. So the control-to-output plant Gd(s) is a second-order low-pass with a complex LC pole pair and a single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C) - and NO right-half-plane zero, exactly like the forward and buck. Every CCM transfer function is the buck result scaled through the transformer: Gd and Gb are n/2 times the buck (the 1/2 is the input-divider factor), the output impedance Zo is identical (independent of n), and the active input impedance Z_C is the buck value divided by n**2*D**2 - the full input impedance Zi is Z_C in parallel with the passive input-capacitor divider Z_B(s) = 2*r_B + 2/(C_B*s). Voltage-mode control with a Type-II/Type-III compensator is straightforward; cross over well below fsw/5 (note the output filter ripple frequency is 2*fsw), or use current-mode to drop the plant to first order. In DCM (R_load > R_lim = 4*L*fsw/(1-D)) the plant collapses to first order and the DC gain becomes load-dependent. Distinctive half-bridge features vs. the forward: the transformer is driven symmetrically in both directions, so it self-resets (no reset/tertiary winding and no D < 0.5 duty limit); each switch blocks the full bus voltage Vin (not (1 + 1/n31)*Vin); and the boundary and ripple carry a doubled effective frequency (R_lim = 4*L*fsw/(1-D), dVout = dI_L/(16*C*fsw)) because both half-cycles deliver energy to the output. Watch for flux-imbalance/DC magnetizing current from asymmetric switch timing (blocking capacitor or current-mode control mitigates it), and add a leakage snubber on the primary. Feedback must cross the isolation barrier (optocoupler + shunt reference, or primary-side regulation). All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switches are replaced by their average current sources and the rectifier diodes by their average voltage sources, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
